nodes.name: Anchor settles in his corner
nodes.description: Anchor goes to his usual spot beneath the wooden table, signaling his familiarity with the quarters.
evidence: Anchor trots to his corner beneath a wooden table.

nodes.name: Marcus presents the keeper logbook
nodes.description: Marcus prepares tea and places a decades-old leather-bound logbook on the table for Elena to examine.
evidence: Marcus sets a kettle on and places on the table a large BROWN LEATHER-BOUND LOGBOOK, its spine worn smooth from decades of handling.

nodes.name: Marcus explains the logbook's lineage
nodes.description: Marcus tells Elena the logbook records generations of lighthouse keepers documenting maritime conditions and emergencies.
evidence:
MARCUS
Every keeper back to the first. Wind. Tide. Vessels. Distress calls.

nodes.name: Elena studies and notes the logbook
aliases: Elena studies and notes the logbook
nodes.description: Elena carefully opens the logbook, observes its multi-generational entries, and records notes in her notebook.
evidence: She makes notes in her green spiral notebook.
The handwriting changes across generations but the format is the same.

nodes.name: Elena questions the 1974 gaps
nodes.description: Elena notices missing entries from 1974 and asks Marcus what happened during that period.
evidence:
ELENA
These gaps in 1974 -- what happened?

nodes.name: Marcus cannot explain the gaps
nodes.description: Marcus says the missing 1974 entries predate his tenure, leaving Elena's question unresolved.

nodes.name: Elena discovers Marcus's wife photo
nodes.description: Elena notices a framed photograph of a younger Marcus standing beside a dark-haired woman and asks if she was his wife.
evidence: Elena notices a framed photograph on the shelf: Marcus younger, beside a woman with dark hair.

nodes.name: Marcus reveals Margaret died
nodes.description: Marcus quietly identifies the woman as Margaret and reveals she died three years earlier from a stroke.
evidence:
MARCUS
(quietly)
Margaret. She passed three years ago. A stroke. Quick, at least.

nodes.name: Elena offers sympathy
nodes.description: Elena responds to Marcus's disclosure about Margaret with an apology and sympathy.

nodes.name: Anchor bonds with Elena
nodes.description: Anchor rests his head on Elena's knee, and she affectionately scratches behind his ear and praises him.
evidence: Anchor rests his black head on Elena's knee. She scratches behind his ear.

nodes.name: Marcus explains Anchor's background
nodes.description: Marcus tells Elena the dog's name is Anchor and that he has been with him for five years after being rescued.
evidence:
MARCUS
His name is Anchor. A rescue. Five years now.

nodes.name: Marcus reveals he has no children
aliases: Marcus reveals he has no children
nodes.description: When Elena asks about nearby family and children, Marcus flatly says he has no children and lives only with Anchor.
evidence:
MARCUS
(flat)
No. No children. It is just Anchor and me.

nodes.name: Marcus serves tea
nodes.description: Marcus pours the tea and sets it on the table, completing his quiet hospitality toward Elena.
evidence: He pours the tea and sets it on the table.

nodes.name: Anchor
nodes.description: Marcus's rescued dog, who settles in his corner and warmly interacts with Elena.
evidence: Anchor trots to his corner beneath a wooden table.
Anchor rests his black head on Elena's knee.
It is just Anchor and me.

evidence: He pours the tea and sets it on the table.
Margaret. She passed three years ago.
